# Multiple simplex cap groups: exact threshold variance and stable examples

Let `d>=2`, `m=d+1`. In barycentric coordinates `sum x_i=1`, the
reference simplex has vertices `e_i` and volume `V`. A nearby physical
simplex has vertex matrix `W`, whose columns sum to one. For finitely
many groups `g`, fix proper caps

    H_(g,i)={x_i>=a_(g,i)},       0<a_(g,i)<1,

and nonnegative multipliers `ell_(g,i)`. Zero multipliers are allowed.
Write `F_(g,i)(W)` for their actual cap volumes and

    L(W)=V det W-sum_(g,i) ell_(g,i) F_(g,i)(W).

The cap groups need not be concurrent for the general formulas.
The examples below include groups which individually are concurrent
full-space covers, as well as an actual two-fiber problem in which
every global cap budget is equal.

## 1. Exact stationarity and the effective threshold

Put

    X_(g,i)=1/(1-a_(g,i)),
    eta_(g,i)=ell_(g,i)(1-a_(g,i))^d,
    e_i=sum_g eta_(g,i),
    chi_i=sum_g eta_(g,i) d(X_(g,i)-1).

For a physical velocity `B`, each column sum is zero. Let `A` be its
off-diagonal part, `b_i=B_ii`, `s_i=sum_(j!=i)A_ij`, and `T=tr B`.
The exact cap formula and its first derivative are

    F_(g,i)(W)/V
      =det W (W_ii-a_(g,i))^d/product_(j!=i)(W_ii-W_ij),

    F_(g,i)'(I)[B]/V
      =(1-a_(g,i))^d [T+s_i+d(X_(g,i)-1)b_i].                (1)

Thus the coefficient of the independent off-diagonal entry `A_ij`
in `L'(I)[B]/V` is

    -1+sum_l e_l-e_i+chi_j.                                  (2)

The same comparison with a third index as in the single-group theorem
shows that stationarity is equivalent to

    e_i=e>0,        chi_i=1-de                 for every i.   (3)

Indeed fixed `j` in (2) forces all other `e_i` equal, and `m>=3`
then makes all `e_i` equal. Nonnegative multipliers make `e>0`;
otherwise every multiplier is zero and (2) cannot vanish.

Use the probability weights `eta_(g,i)/e` at each vertex. Equation
(3) says their means are the SAME number

    mu=E_i X=1/(de)>1.

In particular `0<e<1/d`. Define the effective threshold

    a_*=1-1/mu=1-de in (0,1).                                (4)

The one-group model with threshold `a_*` at every vertex and multiplier
`ell_*=e/(1-a_*)^d` is stationary and has exactly the same first
derivative contribution as all the original groups together. Conversely
(3) suffices for stationarity, without any further groupwise condition.

## 2. The exact threshold-variance correction

Let `Q_*(B)` be the Hessian `L''(I)[B,B]/V` of that single effective
model. Let `sigma_i^2=E_i[(X-mu)^2]`. The full Hessian is exactly

    Q_multi(B)=Q_*(B)-d(d-1)e sum_i sigma_i^2 b_i^2.            (5)

To see every sign and factor, the first and second logarithmic cap
derivatives at a fixed vertex and threshold are

    log F' =T+s_i+d(X-1)b_i,
    log F''=-tr(B^2)-d X^2 b_i^2
                         +sum_(j!=i)(b_i-A_ij)^2.

The mean of the squared first derivative differs from its value at
`X=mu` by `d^2 sigma_i^2 b_i^2`. The mean of the second logarithmic
derivative differs by `-d sigma_i^2 b_i^2`. Since
`F''/F=(log F')^2+log F''`, summing with weight `e` and subtracting
the cap terms in the Lagrangian gives exactly (5).

An explicit formula, if the effective threshold is not canonical, is

    Q_*(B)=T^2-tr(B^2)
       -e sum_i { [T+s_i+d(mu-1)b_i]^2-tr(B^2)
                    -d mu^2 b_i^2+sum_(j!=i)(b_i-A_ij)^2 }.

This is a physical Hessian of actual cap volumes. The correction is
negative semidefinite for nonnegative multipliers. It is zero precisely
on velocities whose `b_i` vanish at every vertex with positive threshold
variance. No comparable sign is asserted for signed multipliers.

## 3. Exact inertia when the effective threshold is canonical

Suppose `e=1/m`, so `a_*=1/m`, and all vertices have the same variance
`sigma^2`. Let `c_j=sum_i A_ij=-b_j`. The audited canonical Hessian
formula gives

    Q_multi(A)=(1/d-theta)||c||^2
                          -(||s||^2+||A||_F^2)/m,
    theta=d(d-1)sigma^2/m.                                   (6)

For clarity, the exact inertia follows from the column-sum minimizing
decomposition in `candidate ca3ec9792c38df0f`.
On its zero-column-sum kernel the form is strictly negative, with
dimension `d^2-1`. The constant column-sum lift has coefficient
`-theta`. The zero-sum column-sum lift has coefficient

    alpha_d-theta,      alpha_d=(d^2-1)/[d(dm-1)].

The three pieces remain orthogonal after adding the correction.
Writing inertia as `(positive, zero, negative)`, it is therefore

    (d,1,d^2-1)      if theta=0;
    (d,0,d^2)        if 0<theta<alpha_d;
    (0,d,d^2)        if theta=alpha_d;
    (0,0,d(d+1))     if theta>alpha_d.                         (7)

Thus threshold variance can remove every canonical positive direction.

## 4. Concurrent cap groups with a negative-definite Hessian in every d>=2

There are `m` groups, indexed by `g`. Put

    a_(g,g)=1-d/(3m),
    a_(g,i)=1/(3m)                 for i!=g.

Every group's thresholds sum to one, so its boundaries pass through
one point and its caps cover the whole barycentric affine span. At
each vertex give the high-threshold cap normalized weight

    eta_H=1/(3m^2),

and each of its `d` low-threshold caps normalized weight

    eta_L=(3m-1)/(3m^2 d).

The actual positive multipliers are `ell=eta/(1-a)^d`.
At each vertex their total is `e=1/m`. The two reciprocal thresholds
are `X_H=3m/d` and `X_L=3m/(3m-1)`; the probability of the high
one is `1/(3m)`. Direct calculation gives

    mu=m/d,
    sigma^2=4m^2/[d^2(3m-1)],
    1/d-theta=-[m(4d-7)+1]/[d(3m-1)]<0.

Equation (6) is consequently negative definite on every nonzero physical
vertex velocity. With the individual budgets fixed at their initial
cap masses, this reference simplex is a strict local volume maximum:
the stationary Lagrangian is strictly smaller at every sufficiently
nearby distinct simplex, and positive multipliers convert feasibility
of all original cap budgets into the corresponding volume bound.

A second simple planar choice is the three permutations of
`(4/5,1/10,1/10)`, with high-threshold multiplier `5/6` and
low-threshold multiplier `5/27`. Then

    e=1/3, mu=3/2, sigma^2=49/36,
    Q=-(11/27)||c||^2-(||s||^2+||A||_F^2)/3.

Its inertia is `(0,0,6)`, rather than the canonical `(2,1,3)`.
On this lone triangle the initial cap budgets are `V/25` and
`81V/100`. They are unequal and cannot all be active at a single
common budget. These examples alone do not address that additional
condition.

## 5. Equal GLOBAL budgets: an actual two-fiber stable example

Here equal global budgets also coexist with a negative-definite physical
Hessian. Take the actual convex body `[0,1] x T_2`; its two positive
integer fibers at bases `z=0,1` are the same triangle of area `V`.
In barycentric coordinates, for every `i=0,1,2`, impose two ambient caps

    H_i^L={x_i>=1/10+(7/10)z},
    H_i^H={x_i>=4/5-(7/10)z}.                                (8)

Each global cap has exactly the SAME initial mass

    B=(81/100+1/25)V=17V/20.                                 (9)

At each integer base the low-threshold triple covers its whole fiber,
so the six caps cover the actual mixed source. No claim of coverage at
every noninteger base is needed. Give every global cap multiplier
`5/11`. Each triangle sees one high and one low threshold at each
vertex, both with this multiplier. Hence for each triangle

    e=17/44,    mu=22/17,    a_*=5/22,
    sigma^2=196/289.

These satisfy the stationarity equations. In the physical off-diagonal
coordinates `(A_01,A_02,A_10,A_12,A_20,A_21)`, the characteristic
polynomial of its normalized Hessian matrix is

    (11 x+6)(11 x+7)(121 x^2+143 x+27)^2 / 1771561.           (10)

Every root is strictly negative: the linear roots are negative and the
quadratic has positive constant and linear coefficients and positive
discriminant `7381`. Equivalently, the leading principal minors of the
negative Hessian are

    13/22, 36/121, 234/1331, 1127/14641,
    12987/322102, 30618/1771561.

The two triangles are independently physically variable, because their
bases are exposed and there is no intermediate integer base. The joint
Lagrangian Hessian is the direct sum of the two negative-definite
blocks. It is therefore a strict local maximum of total volume subject
to all six EQUAL global cap budgets (9). The convex hull of any nearby
pair retains exactly those two integer fibers.

The budget in (9) is NOT the actual critical maximum-depth value.
At either exposed base, other-fiber mass can be excluded by a sufficiently
large finite base tilt. Thus the actual maximum depth of the source is
`Gamma_2 V=4V/9`, attained at either own centroid, and its normalized
value is `2/9`. The common covering budget divided by total mass is
`17/40`, strictly larger. This is an OC-sharp two-fiber source equipped
with noncritical cap constraints; it is not an OC counterexample or a
critical-budget stability example.

Equal global cap masses alone therefore do not preserve the canonical
positive Hessian index. Whether the cap budget is the actual attained
maximum depth is a separate condition not removed by this construction.

The companion `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_multiple_simplex_cap_group_variance.py` checks
the variance identity directly from second-order cap expansions, the
stationary concurrent families, and the exact equal-budget Hessian.
